The foregoing amendment to claim 20 addresses the claim objection raised on page 2 of the Office Action. Accordingly, withdrawal of the objection to claim 20 is respectfully requested.

The power device (1), according to Orita, includes a motor encoder 10 providing an angular position of the motor axle (input side of gear (3)) and an angular differential encoder (11) providing the angular rotational difference of the input side and output side of torsion bar 4. Orita uses the measurement of motor encoder 10 to calculate the angular position of the input side of the torsion bar 4 by converting the angular position of the motor shaft to the angular position of the output side of gear 3 based on the gear ratio (see [ 0092]). Orita does not apply the torque produced by motor 2, that moves gear 3 and rotary member 5, to determine the stiffness at gear 3. Moreover, Orita makes no mention of using a computed angular rotational difference of the input side and output side of torsion bar 4 to assess the stiffness of gear 3. Orita uses the measurement of motor encoder 10 to calculate the angular position of the input side of torsion bar 4 and to convert the angular position of output shaft 2b to the angular position of the output side of gear 3 based on the gear ratio. Therefore, Orita fails to teach or suggest "applying the torque to the motor axle resulting in rotation of the motor axle and the output axle," and "determining the stiffness of the gear based on at least the angular position of the motor axle, the angular position of the output axle," as recited in independent claim 1. For at least this reason, Orita fails to remedy the deficiencies of Klimchik.
Although different in scope, amended independent claims 19 and 35 recite similar
features and are patentable over the cited portions of the applied references for at least the same reasons as explained above with respect to claim 1.
